added: Chevalier and Mayzlin 2006; Dellarocas 2003; Forman et al. 2008

problems.original_quote: these studies found that reviews matter, a one-star increase leads to a 5-9% increase in revenue
problems.revised_quote: with estimates suggesting that a one-star increase in average rating is associated with a 5-9% increase in revenue
problems.explanation: The original states a causal finding ("found", "leads to"); the revision weakens it to a suggested association.

problems.original_quote: remains, to the best of our knowledge, somewhat underexplored in the existing literature
problems.explanation: Dropping both "to the best of our knowledge" and "somewhat" turns a hedged novelty claim into an unhedged one.

problems.original_quote: an investigation of the relationship between online reviews and sales was conducted by several researchers
problems.revised_quote: A substantial literature links online reviews to sales
problems.explanation: The original cites work by "several researchers"; the revision describes it as a "substantial literature", which overstates how much prior evidence exists.

problems.revised_quote: Yet this work treats a review largely as a rating.
problems.explanation: The revision adds a characterization of the prior literature that the original does not make.
"Important" became "direct", which slightly changes how the implications are characterized.

parsed.summary: The revision weakens the causal claim about prior findings and strips the hedges from the novelty claim. It also inflates prior work into a "substantial literature" and adds a new characterization of that literature, so the passage no longer says exactly what the original said.
